issues.description: nevra[0] uses the first character of the filename, not the package name's first letter, breaking when filename has leading non-letter characters
issues.detail: The canonical koji path is .../Packages/<first-letter-of-name>/<nevra.rpm>. Using nevra[0].lower() assumes the filename begins with the package name. If any URL produces a filename starting with a digit or other char (e.g. '389-ds-base-...rpm', '7zip-...rpm'), the subdirectory will be '3' or '7', which matches koji's convention only by accident. State the invariant: 'filename begins with package name, koji subdir is first char of package name' and assert it.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None, producing a malformed URL like '.../latest/None/Packages/...' instead of failing loudly
issues.detail: When the regex doesn't match, the function returns None and the caller interpolates it into the URL via f-string. There is no termination check. A correct algorithm here must either raise or be proven to always match. State the invariant on the input set, then assert it; do not let None propagate into a URL string.

issues.description: Arch regex uses \b but x86_64 and ppc64le contain digits/underscores that interact with \b in surprising ways
issues.detail: In Python's re, \b is between a word char and non-word char; underscore is a word char. So r'\bx86_64\b' inside '/x86_64/' matches, but the author's stated intent ('chars immediately surrounding must be non-word, e.g. /') is not quite what \b enforces. Works in practice for slash-delimited URLs, but the comment overstates the guarantee. Consider anchoring on '/' explicitly for readability.

issues.description: Arch list is hardcoded in two places (here and implicitly in generate_main); single source of truth would help
issues.detail: The supported arch set is a load-bearing constant. Duplicating it locally invites drift when a new arch is added. Hoist to a module-level tuple SUPPORTED_ARCHES and reuse. Small change, improves readability — the reader sees one definition instead of hunting.

issues.description: Function name use_koji_url_only and the comment 'we only want coreos-pool URLs' are slightly misleading
issues.detail: The function does not filter to coreos-pool URLs; it rewrites non-coreos-pool URLs into coreos-pool-shaped URLs under the assumption that koji-tagger will later make them resolvable. A literate name like rewrite_to_coreos_pool_urls plus a one-paragraph comment explaining the race-with-tagger invariant (documented in the PR description but absent from the code) would serve a future reader far better.

issues.description: No unit test accompanies a URL-rewriting function whose correctness depends on string parsing of untrusted-shape inputs
issues.detail: 'Beware of bugs in the above code; I have only proved it correct, not tried it.' This function is pure, deterministic, and trivially testable with a handful of representative URLs (coreos-pool passthrough, fedora x86_64, fedora-secondary ppc64le, edge-case filename). A 20-line test would catch the nevra[0] and None-arch issues above. The PR description even notes local testing is hard — all the more reason to test the parts that are local.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED and NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The rewriting logic is small and the asymptotic complexity is trivially O(n) over the URL list, which is fine. But the algorithm rests on two unstated invariants — (1) the RPM filename's first character equals the package name's first character (koji subdir convention) and (2) every non-coreos-pool URL contains exactly one of four known arches — and neither is asserted in code. extract_arch_from_url silently returns None on miss, which will compose into a malformed URL rather than fail loudly. Add a unit test for the four representative cases, assert the arch is non-None, hoist the arch list to a constant, and write a literate comment that names the race-with-koji-tagger assumption that currently lives only in the PR description.
